title: ISI Mark — What It Means
text: The ISI Mark is India's official quality certification mark issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). A product bearing the ISI Mark has been tested and certified to conform to a specific Indian Standard (IS). Key features: 1. The ISI mark comprises the distinctive logo + IS number + BIS licence number (CM/L-XXXXXXX). 2. Only licensed manufacturers can use the ISI Mark. 3. BIS conducts surprise market surveillance to verify authenticity. 4. Mandatory for 900+ product categories under Quality Control Orders (QCOs). Consumer right: You can verify ISI mark authenticity via BIS Care app or the BIS portal. Source: BIS Act 2016 and BIS Consumer Affairs Division.

title: How to Verify an ISI Mark
text: How to verify an ISI mark: 1. Check for the correct ISI logo (not a hand-drawn imitation). 2. Note the 7-digit CM/L licence number on the product or packaging. 3. Verify using BIS Care App — available on Android and iOS. Enter the licence number to see the licensed manufacturer's details. 4. Verify online at https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification. 5. Call BIS Consumer helpline: 1800-11-4000 (toll-free). Red flags of a fake ISI mark: Missing CM/L number, blurry/smudged mark, IS number not matching product type, no BIS logo. Source: BIS Consumer Affairs Division.

title: How to File a Complaint Against a BIS-Marked Product
text: How to file a complaint with BIS: Online: https://www.bis.gov.in/consumer-affairs/consumer-complaint. Phone: 1800-11-4000 (BIS toll-free helpline, 9am-5:30pm Monday-Saturday). Email: consumer@bis.org.in. In person: Visit nearest BIS Regional/Branch Office. What to provide in complaint: Product name and brand, IS number on the product, CM/L licence number, Batch/lot number (if visible), Purchase details (shop name, date, bill), Description of the defect or harm. Action BIS takes: BIS can raid the manufacturer, seize non-conforming stock, cancel licence, and initiate prosecution under BIS Act 2016. Source: BIS Consumer Affairs Division, BIS Act 2016.

title: Consumer Rights Under BIS Act 2016
text: Consumer rights under BIS Act 2016: 1. Right to buy safe, quality-certified products — mandatory ISI/CRS marking on QCO-covered products. 2. Right to verify: BIS maintains a public database of all licensed manufacturers. 3. Right to complain: BIS is mandated to investigate consumer complaints within 30 days. 4. Penalty for selling substandard ISI-marked products: Up to 2 years imprisonment and ₹2 lakh fine for first offence under Section 29 of BIS Act 2016. 5. Hallmarking fraud: Selling un-hallmarked/mismarked gold jewellery — up to 1 year imprisonment and ₹1 lakh fine. Source: BIS Act 2016, Sections 17, 29, 30.
